newsitem.title: UK: NWE gasoline ends higher, low octanes stay tighter.
newsitem.headline: NWE gasoline ends higher, low octanes stay tighter.

text.p: NWE gasoline prices ended slightly higher on Thursday as regular unleaded continued to hold at narrow levels against premium unleaded in an otherwise thin and uneventful session, traders said.
"The low octanes are less available," said one broker. "When (the spread) gets down toward $5 the refiners sit up and take notice...and at $10 everyone wants to buy it."

Regular unleaded barges ended $1 up at $214/$216 fob ARA and stayed about $5-$6 under Eurograde, which rose $2 to $220/$222. An early Eurograde deal was done at $218 fob ARA but sources said bids were consistently above that level for the day.
That was even though trades were few and far between.

The broker said the arbitrage to the States may still be open for larger vessels, but unlikely for smaller material. One major was seen holding onto barrels offering $216.50 fob with bids at $214, he said.
Gasoline inventories held in independent tankage in the Amsterdam-Rotterdam-Antwerp area rose in the latest week to 550,000-575,000 tonnes, up from week-ago and year-ago levels of 525,000 tonnes.
Industry sources said stocks rose due to incoming components readying to be built into cargoes for trans-Atlantic shipment, and with the contango offering an incentive to store.
